messages:
maria: Heads-up — seeing a ~2m spike in controller-manager reconcile latency in eu-west1. A bunch of gpu-scheduler pods stuck Pending and allocator logs show leader churn.

infra-bot: [ALERT] ctrlmgr_reconcile_latency > 1.0s (eu-west1) — firing at 2023-11-03T10:05:40Z

sam: Can you paste the lease/leader logs from the ctrlmgr pod? sounds like frequent leader flips.

jia: grabbing logs now. snippet: `E1103 10:04:59.124 controller.go:467] failed to renew lease: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = transport is closing` repeated every 10-20s. then `I1103 10:05:20.987 leaderelection.go:243] lock lost`

oliver: curious — any NAT/conntrack drops in the same timeframe? we've seen conntrack exhaustion cause transient grpc drops to etcd in the past.

maria: good call. host conntrack near limit on the GPU node pool NAT gateway: `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` -> 65520 and max is 65536.

sam: that'd explain ephemeral gRPC failures to etcd and lease renew failures. Can we cold-bump conntrack or rotate NAT?

jia: rotating NAT would be noisy. quick mitigation: increase controller-manager lease duration to reduce flips while we investigate. patching now: 
```
kubectl -n kube-system patch deployment kube-controller-manager --type=strategic -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"kube-controller-manager","command":["kube-controller-manager","--leader-elect","--leader-elect-lease-duration=60s","--leader-elect-renew-deadline=40s","--leader-elect-retry-period=10s"]}]}}}}'
```

oliver: also temporarily bump nf_conntrack_max on the NAT hosts and add a short conntrack gc pause: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=131072` — rolling that to the NAT fleet now.

maria: applied the patch, ctrlmgr logs show fewer renew attempts. reconnects drop from ~10/s to 0.2/s. allocator started scheduling queued GPU pods.

deploy-bot: rollout status deployment/kube-controller-manager: 1 of 3 updated.

sam: nice. Still want a root cause — why did conntrack climb so high? any spike in service connections or a customer job pattern?

jia: looking at NetworkFlow logs — large fanout from a batch inference job in eu-west1 around 10:03. many short-lived connections to an internal redis cache. Likely created ephemeral NAT entries faster than GC.

oliver: follow-ups: 1) add conntrack monitoring (rate of new entries) and alert earlier; 2) tune NAT GC and extra headroom for GPU-heavy regions; 3) consider sticky outbound pools for long-running infra flows.

maria: agreed. I'll open a ticket and mark priority P1 for eu-west1 network config. Also add a postmortem note: increasing controller-manager lease is a band-aid that trades quick stability vs. masking underlying network scaling problem (cost consideration: bigger NAT + NAT IPs).

sam: for immediate ops runbook: if ctrlmgr reconcile latency spikes with leader lost messages, check etcd gRPC errors -> check NAT conntrack -> if close to max, either bump nf_conntrack_max or rotate NAT.

jia: infra-bot reports cluster health recovered, pending GPU pods now 0 in queue. will follow up with perf histograms and a brief postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:

oliver: thanks team. leaving a note to discuss longer-term: reduce ephemeral connection fanout from the inference job (dev/product) — that has the best cost/complexity win.
